source: Independent Budget Office, tables on New York City residents' income and income tax liability, tax year 2023 (released Feb. 10, 2026), sheet 2 Summary
basis: Liability before credits, the Independent Budget Office's measure. Tax owed on 2023 returns, not fiscal-year collections.
coverage: City residents' returns only: 3,905,234 returns and $14,630.6 million of liability before credits. Leaves out the pass-through entity tax paid by businesses, which the first chart counts in this line for 2026 and 2027, and refunds, audits and other collections.
sub: The income tax squares, split by the filer's income. Tax year 2023, the latest available: 3.9 million returns and $14.6 billion of tax owed before credits. Click a row to isolate it.

bands.label: $1 million and over
bands.note: Filers with $1 million or more filed 34,307 returns. After refundable credits, mostly for city tax their businesses paid on their behalf, their share is 30%.

more: Income is New York adjusted gross income, the income figure on state tax returns. Filers are tax returns; a married couple filing jointly counts once. Shares of the tax are of tax owed before credits, the measure the Independent Budget Office uses. After refundable credits the top group's share is 30%. Most of the difference is the pass-through entity tax credit: partnerships and S corporations can choose to pay city tax on their owners' income themselves, and the owners then claim a matching credit, so that tax is paid through the business instead. The 2021 peak, when filers with $1 million or more owed 48%, was driven largely by capital gains in a strong stock market, not by a rate change. The city tax applies to residents only.
